key_insight: TAO-DFT shows that ladder-type phenylenes remain singlets but evolve from nonradical to polyradical behavior as the fused-ring length increases, with a damped periodic hotspot pattern at n = 3k - 1.
engineering_relevance: These size-dependent electronic trends help guide the rational design of extended π-conjugated nanomaterials with tunable radical character and electronic functionality.
method: Applied thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) to n-LPs with n = 1–40.
Analyzed ground-state spin character, radicality, and frontier/active orbitals across molecular sizes.
Used real-space active-orbital representations to link electronic behavior to structural localization along the central ladder framework.
evidence_signal: The study systematically evaluated a size series of 40 ladder-type phenylenes and identified consistent singlet ground states plus an oscillatory radical-character pattern with hotspots at n = 3k - 1.
watch_item: TAO-DFT predictions are computational and depend on the chosen functional/occupation model, so experimental validation is still needed for larger or more strongly correlated systems.
paper_title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
